It's also already a known, tracked task: mission-control/NOTES-FOR-CLAUDE.md explicitly lists 'D9 (55 goldens → reviewed:true)' as a founder sign-off item recommended before the pilot outreach build. So the finding is real and correctly characterized, but severity P2 (not P1) is right: it's a human-review/process gap on customer-facing copy, not a crash/security hole/data-loss/silently-wrong-code bug, and it's already surfaced on the board awaiting Dylan's ~30min review pass. The proposal (prioritize chargeback/priority/gift branches, promote the console.log to a CI warning annotation) is low-risk and doesn't touch the repository seam, proof-only doctrine, or hot-file serialization list.

title: Every inbound ingest reads the merchant's entire outcome-event ledger
problem: ingestTicket → recordReplyAttribution calls outcomeEvents.listByMerchant on EVERY inbound (webhook, widget, CSV), pulling the merchant's whole append-only ledger (reply_sent + customer_replied + reopened + csat + resolved_quiet grow forever) and filtering by orderId in JS. There is no orderId index — the Mongo compound index is {merchantId,variantId,kind,observedAt} — so this is an unbounded scan on the webhook fast-ACK path. As the ledger reaches tens of thousands of rows it slows every ingest and eventually breaches the vendor's ~5s webhook timeout.
proposal: Add outcomeEvents.listByOrder backed by a {orderId, observedAt} index and query only this order's events in recordReplyAttribution (it only ever needs one order's reply_sent/reopened rows). Same for the reopen-dedupe check.

verdict.note: Confirmed accurate against code: service.ts recordReplyAttribution (line 326) calls outcomeEvents.listByMerchant then filters by orderId in JS (330-336, 362-364), invoked from ingestTicket on every webhook/widget/CSV inbound (line 485). No listByOrder exists on OutcomeEventRepository (types.ts:122); the only Mongo index on outcome_events is {merchantId,variantId,kind,observedAt} (client.ts:51-53) -- no orderId -- so this is genuinely a full per-merchant scan on every ingest. The proposed fix (add listByOrder backed by an {orderId,observedAt} index, implemented in both json and mongo drivers) is additive, doesn't touch the proof-only doctrine, and is plausible at M effort. Severity downgraded to P2: the stated P1 bar is security hole / data loss / pilot hits it week one / silently wrong results. Nothing here is lost or wrong -- it's a latency/scale defect that only bites once a merchant's append-only ledger reaches tens of thousands of rows, which a solo founder's week-one pilot merchant (low order volume) will not approach. Worth fixing before scale, but not urgent for this week's go-live.

title: Quiet-resolution cron is O(events²) per merchant and permanently starves merchants after the first slow one
problem: sweepResolvedQuiet nests events.some(...) inside for(reply of events) — quadratic in a merchant's full event history — and the route loads the entire ledger per merchant and processes merchants sequentially in ONE request. With months of events the pass exceeds Vercel's max function duration; because merchants are iterated in fixed order, every daily run dies at the same merchant and those after it are never swept, so their quiet-resolution stats silently freeze. Idempotency preserves correctness but not liveness.
proposal: Precompute an orderId→latest-comeback map once (O(E)) instead of events.some per reply, and either shard the cron per-merchant (Vercel cron can hit a per-merchant param) or give each merchant a bounded time budget so a slow one can't starve the rest.

verdict.note: Confirmed as described. lib/outcome-sweep.ts:71-76 nests events.some(...) inside the reply-events for-loop — genuine O(events²) per merchant. route.ts:64-87 awaits repos.outcomeEvents.listByMerchant + the sweep sequentially per merchant in one request, no maxDuration override in vercel.json/route.ts and no per-merchant sharding, so a slow merchant's pass can exhaust the function's time budget. Verified merchant order is NOT incidental: lib/repositories/mongo/repositories.ts:47-52 explicitly sorts by createdAt then id for deterministic order (JSON driver is stable file order too), so the same merchant would die at the same point on every run — the route doc's claim that "a missed run self-heals on the next" (route.ts:23-25) is true only for the merchant that times out, not for the ones after it in fixed order, which never get swept at all. That's a real, silent bug in the code's own reasoning, not an auditor error. Severity: P2 is right, not P1 — this pilot launches with a single merchant this week, and the blowup needs 'months of events' per the auditor's own evidence; no data loss or wrong-result risk (idempotent, correctness preserved), only a liveness/stats-freshness risk that only bites once there are multiple merchants with real history. Fix (precompute orderId→latest-comeback map + per-merchant sharding or time budget) is straightforward and doesn't touch the repository seam or proof-only doctrine — feasible without breaking verify/test gate.

title: DATA_DRIVER defaults to the ephemeral in-memory JSON store — wrong fail-safe for prod
problem: getRepositories() returns the JSON in-memory driver for ANY DATA_DRIVER value other than exactly 'mongo' (unset, 'json', 'mock', or a typo). In production that means writes land in a per-lambda in-memory store that resets on cold start and diverges across concurrent instances — silent data loss and split-brain with no error surfaced. For a paying pilot this is catastrophic and invisible.
proposal: Fail closed: when DEMO_MODE==='false' (or NODE_ENV==='production') and DATA_DRIVER!=='mongo', throw at startup instead of silently using json. (Whether prod actually sets DATA_DRIVER=mongo needs Dylan to confirm in Vercel, but the default should not be the ephemeral driver.)

verdict.note: Confirmed as described. tideover/lib/repositories/index.ts:16-24 defaults to jsonRepositories for any DATA_DRIVER value except exactly "mongo" — unset, "json", "mock", or a typo all silently fall through. RELEASE.md:41-46 documents that prod is *supposed* to set DATA_DRIVER=mongo, but this is a manual Vercel dashboard step with zero code-level enforcement. Checked for guards elsewhere: lib/health.ts:23 reads the same env var and exposes it via /api/health but doesn't fail on json-in-prod; scripts/smoke.mjs (the deploy-gate smoke test) never calls /api/health or asserts driver==="mongo" — it only checks page/API 200s and the proof-only copy tripwire. So a forgotten or mistyped DATA_DRIVER in Vercel would deploy clean, pass smoke, and silently serve every pilot merchant from an ephemeral per-lambda in-memory store (data loss + split-brain across instances), with no error anywhere. Proposal (throw at startup when DEMO_MODE==='false' or NODE_ENV==='production' and driver!=='mongo') is feasible, cheap (effort S), doesn't touch the mongo driver or the JSON driver internals, and doesn't affect DEMO_MODE=true / dev / test paths since NODE_ENV!=='production' there — verify+test gate unaffected. Auditor's own P2 rating is reasonable: this is a one-time deploy-config misconfiguration risk (not a bug hit by normal pilot usage) and Dylan already documents the correct value in RELEASE.md, but it's a real single-point-of-failure with no fail-safe or smoke-test coverage, worth fixing before/soon after go-live. Not bumping to P1 since it requires an env-config mistake to trigger, not a code path a compliant deploy would ever hit — but flagging that adding a smoke-test assertion on /api/health driver would close this cheaply alongside the proposed throw.

title: lib/service.ts is a 938-line, 15-function god module under every hot file but not itself in the serialization list
problem: service.ts orchestrates ingest, drafting/alternates, approve-send, variant promotion, queue, dashboard, script performance, and setup — every designated hot file (inbox page, DraftRail, ApprovalBar, app dashboard page) funnels through this single module. The 'one in-flight change at a time' discipline names the UI hot files but not the shared module they all call, so two agents each told to touch a different named hot file can still collide by editing overlapping functions in service.ts with no serialization rule catching it.
evidence: tideover/lib/service.ts (938 lines; 15 exported functions spanning ingestTicket/regenerateDraft/approveSend/promoteVariant/getQueue/getDashboard/computeScriptPerformance/getSetupChecklist), all five named hot files import from @/lib/service
proposal: Either add lib/service.ts to the explicit hot-file serialization list in CONTRIBUTING.md, or split it along its seams (ingest, send/approve, dashboard/queue read-models, script performance) so unrelated concurrent changes don't share one file.

verdict.note: Core fact checks out: tideover/lib/service.ts is 938 lines with ~13 exported functions (ingestTicket, regenerateDraft, approveSend, promoteVariant, getQueue, getDashboard, computeScriptPerformance, getSetupChecklist, etc.) and CONTRIBUTING.md:38's hot-file serialization list (inbox/page.tsx, DraftRail.tsx, ApprovalBar.tsx, app/page.tsx, lib/engines/reassurance.ts) indeed omits it. But the evidence overstates connectivity: only 2 of the 5 named hot files (app/app/inbox/page.tsx, app/app/page.tsx) actually `import ... from "@/lib/service"` directly — ApprovalBar.tsx, DraftRail.tsx, and reassurance.ts have no direct import. So "every designated hot file... funnels through this single module" is not literally true. More importantly, CLAUDE.md Part 2 already has a general rule — "Never parallelize two agents that write to overlapping files" — which independently covers the exact collision scenario the finding worries about, regardless of whether the file is on the named hot-file list. The named list is a belt-and-suspenders callout for particularly load-bearing UI/engine surfaces, not the sole safeguard against concurrent edits. Given a solo founder (rarely running two agents destructively editing the same backend module in parallel) and an existing general anti-collision rule already mitigating the risk, this is a legitimate but minor documentation/hygiene gap (worth adding service.ts to the explicit list or splitting it, effort S as proposed) rather than a P2 risk that bites in week-one pilot. Downgrading to P3.

title: verifyStatusToken (public status-page auth) has no direct unit test and no driver-parity test
problem: lib/ids.ts's verifyStatusToken gates /status/[token], /api/status/[token], /api/csat/[token], and /api/widget-submit, and is called independently inside both json/repositories.ts:86 and mongo/repositories.ts:122 for order lookup. No test calls verifyStatusToken directly with a tampered signature, a malformed token (missing dot, empty raw/mac), or checks that both drivers' findByToken agree on the same predicate — the README flags 'the drivers must not diverge' as a live constraint with nothing enforcing it. seed-check re-implements its own sign() copy, never the real function. A bug or future driver divergence would misroute or leak one customer's order-status page to a different token holder.
proposal: Add lib/__tests__/ids.test.ts: valid round-trip, tampered signature rejected, malformed token (no dot / empty parts) rejected, and a parametrized test that seeds one order then asserts json and mongo findByToken agree given the same verifyStatusToken output. Cheap — pure crypto, no I/O for the token half.

verdict.note: Facts check out: verifyStatusToken (lib/ids.ts:51-56) is called independently by json/repositories.ts:86 and mongo/repositories.ts:122, and seed-check.mjs:183 reimplements sign() rather than calling verifyStatusToken directly, so there's genuinely no test exercising the real function or asserting driver parity. But the function itself is correct and trivial today (split on '.', empty-part guard, HMAC-SHA256 truncated compare) — this is a coverage gap, not an active bug, security hole, or data-loss risk. No pilot merchant hits this in week one absent a code change; it only bites if someone edits ids.ts or one driver's findByToken later without the other. Downgrading auditor's P1 to P3: worth adding (proposal is cheap, pure-crypto, no I/O, doesn't touch hot files or the seam) but not urgent/blocking for this week's launch.
